subject: ADR-193: the brief -- a goal hands over every value its task enters and holds exactly what the grader scores, so the next blind trial is a hard one rather than an unfair one
body: ADR-187 SAID THE MISSES WERE THE TASKS' FAULT AND MOVED ON. The number: across the 21 science tasks, 547 values entered and 281 of them appearing nowhere in the goal handed to the operator -- 51% of the data withheld from the people being marked on it. A goal becomes a brief: `says` (the prose, unchanged -- not one of the 55 sentences was rewritten), `gives` (every value the task supplies, with the control that takes it and whether it is bulk) and `holds` (every reading it holds, with its claims). Both new parts are DERIVED FROM THE STEPS, never typed, so a task edited without its brief cannot leave the brief lying. brief_of(claims=False) is the blind brief -- the data without the answers -- and the DEFAULT is the full one so an organiser who forgets the flag notices. What a brief holds is exactly what grade_outcomes scores, step for step and claim for claim, held against ADR-187's four real traces. Exposed on the command line and NOT as a gateway action: a door that served a client its own task would end the blind trial that made the brief necessary. verify_brief 31 (new), mutate_brief 14/14 (new) -- its own suite because it opens nothing and runs in 0.3s, where the same checks in verify_tasks would make a mutant runner twelve hours. Board: 642 values handed over, 632 readings and 1,956 claims held. No goal sentence, page or task step was edited.
